column1: # What the differential test compares, and where each file came from.
# Columns: role, source (tag:path, a release asset, or the path in this repo), sha256 of the bytes.
# v1.3.0 is the newest published release; there is no dev pre-release. Its reader is
# src/ObraDinnHeadTracking/Config/ConfigManager.cs, which takes no core source: its defaults are
# literals. The frozen reader in src/ObraDinnHeadTracking/Legacy is that file restructured to fill
# LegacyConfig and write nothing, so comparison 1 is not empty by construction and runs on every input.

column2: vendor/bepinex/BepInEx_win_x86.zip (BepInEx 5.4.23.5), whose BepInEx.dll the test and the harness below run

column1: # No published build shipped the plugin .cfg, in a ZIP or as a launcher-manifest.json seed (every
# seed is BepInEx/config/BepInEx.cfg), so the inputs are what each build writes at its first start.
# A first-run file is the .cfg that build's own ObraDinnHeadTracking.dll, taken from its release
# ZIP, writes when its ConfigManager.Initialize runs on a ConfigFile at a path with no file and
# the plugin's BepInPlugin metadata: the published binary run once under the BepInEx above, with
# the Unity stubs of pixi run setup-libs. The "Acceptable values" comment lines list the stub's
# KeyCode members, not the game's; no reader reads a comment line. Predecessor builds are
# itsloopyo/obra-dinn-headtracking-old2, whose v1.0.1 to v1.0.5 releases have no tag left. Its
# v1.0.5 DLL declares version 1.0.4, so its first-run file equals the v1.0.4 one.
